content: 1. Before providing comments on the draft recommendations and guideline document, it is essential to submit a current curriculum vitae. 2. The World Health Organization (WHO) has published guidelines on potassium intake for adults and children. 3. The Dietary Guidelines Advisory Committee has released a report on dietary guidelines for Americans. 4. A meta-analysis of randomized controlled clinical trials by Whelton PK, He J, Cutler JA, et al., has examined the effects of oral potassium on blood pressure. 5. The WHO provides resources on cardiovascular diseases, including guidelines and reports. 6. The WHO Guidelines Review Committee has developed a handbook for guideline development. 7. The GRADE system, developed by Guyatt GH, Oxman AD, Vist GE, et al., offers a consensus on rating the quality of evidence and the strength of recommendations. 8. A joint WHO/FAO expert consultation report discusses diet, nutrition, and the prevention of chronic diseases. 9. Research by van Mierlo LA, Greyling A, Zock PL, et al., highlights the impact of suboptimal potassium intake on population blood pressure. 10. The INTERMAP study, led by Stamler J, Elliott P, Dennis B, et al., provides background, aims, design, methods, and descriptive statistics related to dietary and non-dietary factors. 11. Elliott P has prepared a background document on global sodium intakes for a forum on reducing salt intake in populations. 12. Mackay J and Mensah G authored The Atlas of Heart Disease and Stroke, providing insights into cardiovascular health. 13. Murray CJ, Lauer JA, Hutubessy RC, et al., conducted a global and regional analysis of the effectiveness and costs of interventions to lower systolic blood pressure and cholesterol. 14. The WHO has published a global status report on noncommunicable diseases. 15. Strong K, Mathers C, Leeder S, et al., explored the potential lives saved through chronic disease prevention. 16. Chen X and Wang Y conducted a systematic review and meta-regression analysis on blood pressure tracking from childhood to adulthood. 17. Daniels SR, Loggie JM, Khoury P, et al., studied left ventricular geometry and severe left ventricular hypertrophy in children and adolescents with essential hypertension. 18. Young DB examined the role of potassium in preventive cardiovascular medicine. 19. The American College of Sports Medicine, led by Sawka MN, Burke LM, et al., issued a position stand on exercise and fluid replacement. 20. Fukumoto T, Tanaka T, Fujioka H, et al., investigated differences in sweat composition induced by thermal exposure and running exercise. 21. Sawka MN and Montain SJ reviewed fluid and electrolyte supplementation for exercise heat stress. 22. Webster JL, Dunford EK, Neal BC conducted a systematic survey of sodium content in processed foods. 23. Bourges H, Casanueva E, Rosado J provided recommendations on nutrient intake for the Mexican population. 24. The Expert Group on Vitamins and Minerals revised their review of potassium. 25. Dietary reference intakes for the Spanish population were outlined in a report. 26. The Hoge Gezondheidsraad published revised dietary recommendations for Belgium. 27. The INTERSALT Cooperative Research Group conducted an international study on electrolyte excretion and blood pressure, focusing on 24-hour urinary sodium and potassium excretion. 28. The Ministry of Health issued Ordinance No. 23 in 2005, establishing dietary reference intakes for the population. 29. The Korean Nutrition Society and the Ministry of Health & Welfare published dietary reference intakes for Koreans. 30. D’Elia L, Barba G, Cappuccio FP, et al., performed a meta-analysis on potassium intake, stroke, and cardiovascular disease. 31. Geleijnse JM, Kok FJ, Grobbee DE conducted a meta-regression analysis on blood pressure response to changes in sodium and potassium intake. 32. Rabelink TJ, Koomans HA, Hene RJ, et al., studied early and late adjustments to potassium loading in humans. 33. Siani A, Strazzullo P, Giacco A, et al., demonstrated that increasing dietary potassium intake reduces the need for antihypertensive medication. 34. The EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition, and Allergies provided an opinion on the tolerable upper intake level of sodium. 35. Oberleithner H, Callies C, Kusche-Vihrog K, et al., found that potassium softens vascular endothelium and increases nitric oxide release. 36. Cook NR, Obarzanek E, Cutler JA, et al., examined the joint effects of sodium and potassium intake on cardiovascular disease in the Trials of Hypertension Prevention follow-up study. 37. Yang Q, Liu T, Kuklina EV, et al., analyzed sodium and potassium intake and mortality among US adults using data from the Third National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. 38. Chang HY, Hu YW, Yue CS, et al., evaluated the effect of potassium-enriched salt on cardiovascular mortality and medical expenses in elderly men. 39. Kawasaki T, Itoh K, Kawasaki M studied the reduction in blood pressure with sodium-reduced, potassiumand magnesium-enriched mineral salt in individuals with mild essential hypertension. 40. Brown IJ, Tzoulaki I, Candeias V, et al., reviewed global salt intakes and their implications for public health. 41. Dickinson HO, Nicolson DJ, Campbell F, et al., assessed potassium supplementation for managing primary hypertension in adults. 42. The WHO published its 47th edition of basic documents. 43. The WHO issued guidelines for the declaration of interests for WHO experts. 44. The WHO evaluated the effects of increased potassium intake on blood pressure, renal function, blood lipids, and other potential adverse effects. 45. The WHO analyzed the impact of increased potassium intake on cardiovascular disease, coronary heart disease, and stroke. 46. The WHO studied the effects of increased potassium intake on blood pressure and potential adverse effects in children. 47. Chobanian AV, Bakris GL, Black HR, et al., authored the Seventh Report of the Joint National Committee on Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Treatment of High Blood Pressure (JNC 7). 48. Stamler J, Elliott P, Chan Q, et al., provided appendix tables for the INTERMAP study in the Journal of Human Hypertension. 49. Lewington S, Clarke R, Qizilbash N, et al., conducted a meta-analysis on the age-specific relevance of usual blood pressure to vascular mortality. 50. Desai M, Stockbridge N, Temple R discussed blood pressure as a biomarker functioning as a surrogate. 51. Vasan RS reviewed biomarkers of cardiovascular disease, focusing on molecular basis and practical considerations. 52. Geleijnse JM, Grobbee DE, Hofman A studied sodium and potassium intake and blood pressure changes in childhood. 53. The European Union published data on energy and nutrient intake in its member countries. 54. Cook NR, Cohen J, Hebert PR, et al., explored the implications of small reductions in diastolic blood pressure for primary prevention. 55. McPherson K, Britton A, Causer L estimated the impact of changes in risk factors on coronary heart disease. 56. Cashel K, English R, Lewis J provided data on the composition of foods in Australia. 57. Food composition databases for European member countries were compiled. 58. Wu Leung W published food composition data for use in Africa. 59. Wu Leung W, Butrum R, Chang F, et al., provided food composition data for use in East Asia. 60. The Food and Agricultural Organization (FAO) published a report in 2011. 61. The United States Department of Agriculture provided dietary guidelines and food composition data.
